# tesoro

> An Autonomous Economic Governance Layer (AEGL) for AI agents: it decides whether an agent may spend, before it spends, and records which control decided. Deterministic engines, no model in the decision path, integer money, append-only hash-chained evidence.

- Package: https://pypi.org/project/tesoro/ (version 0.1.2, Apache-2.0)
- Source: https://github.com/tesoro-labs/tesoro
- Standard: https://github.com/tesoro-labs/aegs (AEGS 0.1: 12 sections, 90 clauses, 151 executing test vectors)

## Pages

### Start here
- [Evaluate this in ten minutes](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/evaluate.html): A reviewer's page. The narrow claim and the prior art it concedes, the four things this refuses to build, the two attacks that still succeed, and the conformance profile the reference implementation deliberately fails. Every number is reproducible.

### Concepts
- [Autonomous economic governance](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/): An autonomous agent that can pay is an agent that can overpay. What an Autonomous Economic Governance Layer is, and why existing controls do not fit.
- [Four kinds of AEGL](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/types.html): Per-payment cap, cumulative envelope, governed budget, behavioural. Ordered by what each can express, and where the useful boundary falls.
- [The shared vocabulary](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/vocabulary.html): The words this documentation uses precisely: two channels, four verdicts, thirteen controls, envelopes, and the four states.
- [Stablecoins & irreversibility](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/stablecoins.html): AI agents pay in stablecoins like USDC over rails such as x402. A stablecoin payment cannot be reversed, charged back or disputed, so the only place to intervene is before it happens. What that changes about spend controls.
- [Where the obligations fall](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/regulation.html): GENIUS binds permitted payment stablecoin issuers, MiCA binds EMT and ART issuers and CASPs, the Travel Rule binds VASPs. Tesoro is a library and is none of those. Context for an obliged entity, and no compliance claimed.
- [What governs what](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/ecosystem.html): Agent governance splits into layers: what an agent may do, and what an agent may pay. How Tesoro relates to Microsoft's Agent Governance Toolkit, OPA, guardrails and observability tools, and what each is actually for.

### Tesoro
- [What Tesoro is](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/tesoro.html): One implementation of an AEGL: ten deterministic engines, no model in the decision path, attribution on every decision, and an honest list of what it does not do.
- [The benchmark](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/benchmark.html): A reproducible adversarial benchmark for autonomous economic governance. 20 attacks, four outcomes, sealed measurements. Currently 17 defended, 1 defended by accident, 2 undefended — and the two open ones are published rather than hidden.
- [Architecture](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/architecture.html): Ten deterministic engines, the decision path, narrowing, evidence, and why no model sits on it.
- [Policies & rules](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/policies.html): Policy packs are data, never code. The fixed vocabulary, the rule shape, envelopes, and profiles.
- [Frameworks & rails](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/frameworks.html): Claude Agent SDK, Google ADK, LangGraph, CrewAI, and the three-call contract that needs none of them.

### The standard
- [AEGS](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/aegs.html): Thirteen sections, 95 clauses, 167 test vectors, and a suite that scores anything emitting Decision Records.

### Practice
- [Get started](https://tesoro-labs.github.io/tesoro/start.html): Install to a first refusal in about five minutes. No wallet, no testnet, no model key.
